setting.name: Display of Username During Sign-In
setting.casual_explanation: After someone enters their credentials, Windows can keep showing the username or hide it. This setting decides whether the username stays visible during that sign-in flow.
setting.why_people_change_it: People hide the username at sign-in to reduce on-screen identity exposure in shared spaces or environments where shoulder surfing is a concern.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: Hiding the username improves privacy during sign-in, but it also removes a small confirmation cue that can help users notice which account is being used.
setting.professional_notes: Microsoft documents this as the security option 'Interactive logon: Do not display username at sign-in'. The current app writes HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System\DontDisplayUserName = 1, and local Windows security metadata in sceregvl.inf confirms that exact value name for the documented option. The nearby DontDisplayLockedUserId entry is a separate security-option surface and does not change this mapping.

evidence.title: KVM ETW summary receipt for DontDisplayUserName
evidence.summary: A bounded 2026-04-27 ETW retry for `DontDisplayUserName` never reached trace collection. QGA guest-exec failed during guest-dir setup, the runner fell back to send-key launch, and the fallback still timed out in `ensure-admin-shell` before any ETW artifact reached the host.

evidence.title: QGA-first ETW stackwalk runtime receipt for DontDisplayUserName
evidence.summary: A 2026-05-07 QGA-first ETW stackwalk rerun produced ETL/XML artifacts and normalized 4776 registry events with 685 caller-stack events. The bundle contains an exact helper-triggered `RegQueryValue` for `HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Policies\System` / `DontDisplayUserName`, returning `0xC0000034` on the clean baseline.

evidence.title: Guest Ghidra launch receipt for DontDisplayUserName
evidence.summary: A same-day fast guest Ghidra retry for `DontDisplayUserName` failed in `ensure-admin-shell` with a bounded timeout, so no xref bundle reached the host.

decision.why: Microsoft documents the sign-in privacy behavior and the guest-side VM probe confirmed that sceregvl.inf exposes DontDisplayUserName as the registry surface for this option. The app already writes that exact value, so the record is now validated.

validation_proof.notes: Guest-side probe on Win25H2Clean confirmed that sceregvl.inf contains the DontDisplayUserName mapping for the documented sign-in privacy option. DontDisplayLockedUserId also appears in the same file, but it is a separate nearby security-option surface.

source_enrichment.notes: A bounded 2026-04-27 ETW retry for `DontDisplayUserName` never reached trace collection. QGA guest-exec failed during guest-dir setup, the runner fell back to send-key launch, and the fallback still timed out in `ensure-admin-shell` before any ETW artifact reached the host. A same-day fast guest Ghidra retry for `DontDisplayUserName` failed in `ensure-admin-shell` with a bounded timeout, so no xref bundle reached the host. A 2026-05-07 QGA-first ETW stackwalk rerun cleared the earlier QGA/send-key blocker and produced an exact helper-triggered `RegQueryValue` for `DontDisplayUserName` with caller-stack capture.
